hero.h1: Study apps for the exams that qualify people to work
hero.lead: BiDaFa Ltd builds practice and revision apps for occupational licensing and certification exams: the tests people sit before they can work as a notary, a security guard, a tradesperson or a licensed operator.
hero.status: Our first apps are in development and are not yet available to download.

exams.heading: Exam reference pages
exams.intro: Free reference pages for the exams themselves, with every figure cited to the regulator and dated. These are published whether or not an app of ours exists for the exam.

entries.label: FAA Part 107 exam (Unmanned Aircraft General - Small, UAG)
entries.summary: 60 questions, 2 hours, 70 percent to pass. Topic weightings from the FAA Airman Certification Standards, the operating limits from 14 CFR 107.51, and five worked sample questions.

what_we_do.heading: What we do
paragraphs: Occupational licensing exams decide whether someone is allowed to do their job. They are set from published statutes, regulations and official training manuals, they are often sat once or twice a year, and failing one can cost a person a season of work.

The study material for them is frequently poor. BiDaFa Ltd exists to build the practice apps those candidates actually need: accurate, specific to one jurisdiction and one exam, and derived from the official source rather than from a general purpose question bank.
We publish the exam reference pages free, and we publish the method we use to write questions, because a claim about accuracy that cannot be checked is worth nothing.

how_we_build.heading: How we build
how_we_build.intro: These are the principles our apps are designed to, not claims about products in the store. Nothing of ours has launched yet.

principles.h: Built from the official source material
principles.p: Questions are written from the published rules, statutes and training manuals the exam itself is set from, with the source recorded, rather than from guesswork about what might come up.
A wrong answer only teaches you something if you learn why it was wrong, so each question carries an explanation rather than a bare score at the end.
Apps are designed to work offline and to be a single purchase, with no subscription, so revising does not depend on having a signal in the exam centre car park.

about.heading: About the company
paragraphs: BiDaFa Ltd was incorporated in England on 8 August 2026 and is registered as a business and domestic software development company, number 17388837.
It is a small independent company. The research, the writing and the building are done in house, which is the reason we can be specific about a single jurisdiction rather than general about many.

methodology.seo_title: How BiDaFa writes and checks exam questions | BiDaFa Ltd
methodology.seo_description: The method BiDaFa Ltd uses to write practice questions for licensing exams: which documents each question is drawn from, how the source is recorded per question, how figures are checked and dated, and how to report an error.

hero.h1: How we write and check exam questions
hero.lead: This page describes the process, so that a claim about accuracy can be checked rather than taken on trust. It describes how we work today, on material we have built. It is not a claim about a shipped product, because we do not have one yet.

sections.h: Every question is written from a named source document
paragraphs: For each exam we identify the documents the exam itself is set from: the regulation, the awarding body's published standards, and the official study guide where one exists. For the FAA Part 107 exam those are 14 CFR part 107, the Remote Pilot Airman Certification Standards FAA-S-ACS-10B, and the FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide FAA-G-8082-22.

Questions are written from the text of those documents. They are not collected from candidates, not scraped from other question banks, and not recalled from a real sitting. We do not publish or sell real exam questions, and we would not, because doing so breaches the awarding body's terms and teaches recall rather than understanding.

sections.h: Each question records the passage it came from
paragraphs: A question is stored with a reference to the specific section it was drawn from, for example 14 CFR 107.51(b), together with the passage text itself. That reference travels with the question into the explanation, so a candidate who doubts an answer can go and read the rule.
This is also what makes review possible at scale. When a source document changes, the questions attached to the changed section can be found directly instead of by rereading the whole bank.

sections.h: Figures are checked against the source and dated
paragraphs: Any number stated as fact, a fee, a pass mark, a question count, a time limit, carries the source that states it and the date it was last checked. Where the regulator publishes a figure as approximate, we repeat it as approximate rather than rounding it into something that looks more precise than it is.
A figure we cannot source does not go on the page at all. That rule is enforced by the build: the site will not compile if a published figure is not tied to a listed source.

Where we state the size of a question bank, the figure is the honest count of questions written for that exam. We do not inflate a bank size by counting filler, and any derived total is derived from the honest count.

We publish no download numbers, user numbers, ratings, testimonials or pass rates, because we have none. When we have them and can evidence them, we will publish them with their source, and not before.

If you find a mistake on a reference page or in a question, email the address below with the page and the specific figure or question. Reports about a factual error take priority over everything else we are doing.
Corrections are made to the source data and the page is rebuilt, and the check date on the affected page moves to the date of the correction.

We do not describe ourselves as approved, endorsed or affiliated by any regulator or awarding body, because we are not. We do not claim to be the best, the most accurate or the most up to date, because those are not statements anyone can check.
We do not publish reviews or ratings we have solicited, and we will not ask anyone to write one.
